fields.briefDescription: Encrypted delivery, permanent version licenses, and approved creator revenue splits for locally installed Agent Skills, using Solana USDC escrow.
fields.buildingAndAudience: SkillSeal packages reusable Agent workflows with version licenses and approved creator shares. Its website provides upload/preview, signed collaborator approval, operator inspection and share pages; the independent CLI installs locally. Free MIT Skills need no buyer wallet. The hosted Devnet API escrows test USDC, atomically pays collaborators and records a wallet/version grant before key delivery. Public HTTPS purchase, exact 70/30 payouts, five-file installation, no-second-payment reinstall, browser session ZIP recovery, real ten-minute timeout refund and encrypted off-host paid-vault restoration passed. Phantom browser purchase and exact ZIP recovery also passed. The key service is trusted, and decrypted files can be copied. Test accounts are not customers or revenue.
fields.whyAndWhyNow: Agent workflows increasingly combine prompts, reference material, and reusable instructions into locally installed packages. We want to test whether creators can sell those packages while preserving local use and sharing revenue with collaborators. SkillSeal focuses first on developers who already use wallets, rather than assuming every buyer wants crypto payments. Solana makes the approved split and wallet/version receipt inspectable, while encryption and the installer handle delivery. Ordinary payment systems can offer similar access control; our hypothesis is that wallet-native teams value transparent collaboration accounting and purchase recovery. We have not established paying demand. The next experiment is to observe a small group of developers purchasing and reinstalling a useful Skill, measure failures and total costs, and distinguish interest from actual payment commitments.
fields.technologies: Solana; Anchor/Rust escrow program; SPL Token and Devnet USDC; TypeScript; Next.js 16 and React 19; Node.js 24; SQLite; AES-256-GCM; libsodium X25519 sealed boxes; @solana/web3.js; Phantom/Solflare wallet integration; pnpm; GitHub Actions. OpenAI Codex assisted implementation, review, tests, and documentation. The current prototype does not require an LLM API to buy or install a Skill.
